Pliable

PLY-uh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pliable is easily bent or shaped; readily influenced or persuaded.

The gymnastics coach stretched the young athletes daily, insisting that pliable muscles were far less likely to tear during a difficult routine.

Worked Example

Political opponents accused the young senator of being too pliable, bending his position on the bill every time a new donor called.

Pliable can describe something physically bendable, like leather or wire, or -- often less flatteringly -- a person whose opinions bend too easily under pressure.

How Pliable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flexible

flexible: easily bent without breaking

impressionable

impressionable: easily influenced, especially by other people's opinions

Antonyms

rigid

rigid: stiff and unable to bend

inflexible

inflexible: unwilling to change or be persuaded

How Strong Is It? — adaptable → pliable → spineless

adaptable vs. pliable

adaptable vs. pliable: Adaptable just means able to adjust to new situations -- it doesn't necessarily mean someone else is doing the bending.

spineless vs. pliable

spineless vs. pliable: Spineless goes even further than pliable, describing someone with no firm convictions left to bend at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of pliable.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pli

Root — pli: to fold, to bend (from Latin plicare, 'to fold,' filtered through French plier)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be (Latin -abilis)

Put it together

Put it together: Pliable combines pli ('to fold, to bend,' from Latin plicare) with -able. The same root, in disguise, shows up in comply -- literally 'to fold together with' someone else's wishes. To be pliable is to be foldable, in body or in will.

Use the root in a new word: comply

Use the root in a new word: comply: The restaurant had thirty days to comply with the new health-code regulations.

Word Choice

Pliable can be neutral or even useful when describing materials (pliable wire, pliable leather), but applied to a person's opinions or will, it often carries a mild criticism -- suggesting someone bends too easily to outside pressure.
